correctness.rationale: For n>=2, every weight-two word w_{i,j} yields weight-one descendants at i and j-1, hence L+2S<=n-1 for any deletion code. Adjacent pairs starting at consecutive positions collide in a weight-two descendant, so L<=ceil((n-1)/2). It follows that |C|<=floor((3n-2)/4). The explicit even-start adjacent pair words and every gap-three pair at (4h+1,4h+4) achieve that count: weight-one outputs partition even starts and disjoint odd pairs; weight-two outputs are separated by gap or first-one location. This proves the exact all-n optimum, including n=2. Standard-library checker replays all finite boundary/collision checks to n=200 (as documented), with exact finite independent-set search n=2..8; finite checks are not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The claim is an exact all-length independence-number formula for the binary weight-two single-deletion graph. Direct full-text review of Sloane (2002) and Cullina–Kulkarni–Kiyavash (2012) identifies unrestricted code bounds and optimal colorings, neither stating nor implying the exact induced-subgraph maximum. Searches for constant-weight two single-deletion code maxima, equivalent independence formulations and tables did not identify an equivalent result. Historical absolute priority remains uncertain.

value.rationale: An exact maximum for the first nontrivial fixed Hamming weight under single deletion is an intrinsic synchronization-coding parameter. The result determines alpha(L_{1,n,2}) for all n and gives explicit optimal codebooks of size 3n/4+O(1), reducing a graph-packing problem to a sharp elementary resource bound. It is neither an arbitrary slice nor a result automatically implied by known coloring numbers.
